runs.reply:
I haven't changed any code yet. Because this is a full redesign and you didn't specify a look, the first step is choosing a direction, so here are three. Nothing will be written until you pick one.

**What I looked at.** Seedkeep is one screen in `src/App.jsx`: three loans, a search box that filters by seed variety, and a **Return** button for loans that are still out. Right now it looks like a generic template: a white header, white cards on a gray background, an indigo button and pastel status pills. Every direction below keeps the same functions: the list of loans, the variety search, the On loan / Returned status, and marking a loan returned.

**Research.** The screen-reference sources (Refero, Mobbin) aren't connected, so I didn't study any comparable real products. I used 21st.dev component previews and looked at each image myself: a records table, tabs with count badges, a table with status pills, a layered card stack and a stack that switches between layouts. I also drew on things the volunteers already handle at a seed library: the paper loan ledger, library card-catalog drawers, and the seed packets themselves.

---

### A — The Loan Ledger
`Energy 1 · Density 3 · Motion 1 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - [Records Table](https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table): tight rows, a count shown in the footer, and quieter gray text when a field is empty.
  - [Tabs with Count Badge](https://21st.dev/@coss.com/components/tabs-count-badge): tabs labelled On loan · Returned · All, each with a count.
  - A volunteer's paper loan ledger.
- **Look:** Each loan is a ruled row: variety, borrower, date out, status, action. Dates use evenly spaced digits so they line up in a column. Off-white paper background with ink-colored text. There's a single accent color, and it's used only on the Return action.
- **Signature:** Returning a loan stamps the row with a "RETURNED · 1 Oct" ink mark. The row stays in place instead of disappearing.
- **Avoids:** cards, shadows, and pills on every row.
- **Tradeoff:** Fast and clear, but quiet. The screen won't have much personality.

### B — Seed Packet Wall
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 2 · Fidelity low`

- **References:**
  - Paper seed packets (an illustrated front, sowing details on the back).
  - Botanical labels from seed catalogues.
  - [Streaming Data Rows](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows): status labels that pair an icon with text, so status doesn't rely on color.
- **Look:** Each loan is a packet-shaped tile with a folded top edge. The tile is tinted by crop family (tomato, bean, cucumber), and the variety name is set large in a serif typeface. A large search field heads a "What's out this season" summary showing counts.
- **Signature:** A returned packet's flap reads "seed saved".
- **Avoids:** a generic grid of rounded cards on gray.
- **Tradeoff:** It has a lot of character but shows fewer loans per screen, so it gets harder to scan as the list grows.

### C — Card Catalogue Drawer
`Energy 4 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`

This one is built closely on two existing components:
- [Layered Stack](https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack): slightly tilted cards that settle into a neat grid.
- [Morphing Card Stack](https://21st.dev/@koustubhayadiyala36/components/morphing-card-stack): a switch that moves between stack, grid and list layouts.

What it takes from them:
- **Layout:** loans as index cards filed in a drawer, with alphabetical tab dividers.
- **Hierarchy:** the variety on the card's header line, and the borrower and date written in a handwritten-style face.
- **Spacing:** cards overlap slightly, like a real drawer.
- **Interaction:** a switch between "drawer" and "list" views, where search narrows the drawer.
- **Motion:** cards re-shuffle when search changes the list, and a returned card slides out of the "on loan" section.
- **Visual treatment:** not taken; I'd use a cream card stock and red rule lines of my own.

- **Signature:** the drawer itself. You thumb through loans the way you would a real card catalogue.
- **Avoids:** a flat list and generic status badges.
- **Tradeoff:** The most memorable option and the most work to build. The motion needs a reduced-motion fallback, and the overlapping cards make the mobile layout and keyboard navigation harder.

---

**Which do you want: A, B, C, or a mix** (e.g. "A's ledger layout with B's packet typography")? Once you choose, I'll write a short pre-build check and then the code. You can also name a real product or page for C to follow more closely.

The screenshots I took of the references are in `.playwright-mcp/` in the project. I wanted to add that folder to `.git/info/exclude` so they stay out of git, but that edit needs your permission, so they aren't excluded yet.

runs.reply:
Nothing is built yet. I looked at the current app and did the research, and there are three possible directions below. You pick one before I write any UI code, because a redesign this size depends on that choice.

**What I'm designing for:** Seedkeep is a small React and Vite app with no design system. Volunteers use it to log which seed packets are on loan, who has them, since when, and to mark them returned. The new design is built around those real things: packets, borrowers, dates and the end-of-season return. Since you want something visually rich, the most restrained option below is still polished and characterful.

**Research:** Only 21st.dev was connected. Refero and Mobbin weren't, so I didn't look at any shipped full-product screens. I judged each reference by its preview image, and saved those previews in `.design/refs/`, which is untracked.

---

### A: Circulation Desk
`Energy 2 · Density 3 · Motion 2 · Fidelity medium`
- **References:** [Project Index](https://21st.dev/@ssychui/components/project-index), whose rows dim the others on hover and show a cover image next to the cursor. Also [Editorial Testimonial](https://21st.dev/@jatin-yadav05/components/editorial-testimonial), for its oversized, pale index numbers beside large text.
- **Visual character:** Modelled on a library card catalogue. Each loan is a ruled index row: the variety name in a large serif, then borrower and date-out in a small typewriter-style face. The background is warm off-white card stock with a single ink colour plus a rubber-stamp red. Pale accession numbers (`No. 014`) sit in the margin.
- **Signature:** Marking a packet returned presses a crooked "RETURNED · 12 OCT" date stamp onto the row.
- **Avoids:** Cards, pills and shadows.
- **Tradeoff:** The quietest of the three. Its richness comes from type and texture, not motion.

### B: The Packet Deck *(based mainly on two references)*
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`
- **References:** [Motion Card Stack](https://21st.dev/@motiondotdev/components/motion-card-stack), a swipeable stack where the top card moves to the back. [Layered Stack](https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack), a messy fanned deck that tidies into a grid.
- **What it takes from them:**
  - *Composition:* loans on screen as a physical, overlapping stack of packets (Card Stack).
  - *Hierarchy:* the top packet is the main focus and the rest peek out behind it (Card Stack).
  - *Spacing rhythm:* the slightly rotated, loose layout of the deck and grid (Layered Stack).
  - *Interaction:* drag or swipe the top packet, or use the keyboard. You can also switch between a fanned deck and a tidy grid (both references).
  - *Motion:* spring-based dragging and smooth rearranging when the deck becomes a grid.
  - *Visual treatment:* not taken. Their dark photo look is replaced with printed seed packets.
- **Visual character:** Each loan is drawn as a seed packet: a coloured paper envelope with a flat illustration, a heavy condensed name on the front and the borrower written on the flap. Each packet's colour comes from the crop (aubergine for Cherokee Purple, yellow for lemon cucumber). The background is kraft paper.
- **Signature:** Drag a packet into a "Seed returned" envelope slot to mark it returned. There's also a normal button for keyboard and screen-reader users.
- **Avoids:** Feeling like a dashboard.
- **Tradeoff:** Scanning many loans is slower in deck mode, so the grid mode has to do that job. It also needs the `motion` library as a new dependency.

### C: Season Almanac
`Energy 4 · Density 2 · Motion 4 · Fidelity low`
- **References:** [Hero Shutter Text](https://21st.dev/@daiwiikharihar/components/hero-shutter-text) for a huge sliced headline. [Stacking Cards](https://21st.dev/@danielpetho/components/stacking-cards), where cards pin and scale down over each other as you scroll. [Interactive List Preview](https://21st.dev/@hyperiux/components/interactive-list-preview) for a full-width hover band.
- **Visual character:** Scrolling moves through the growing season as one long timeline, from sowing to seed-saving. A very large heading names the season ("SPRING 2026"). Loans are pinned at the month they went out and stack up as you scroll. The colour shifts from soil brown to green to harvest gold.
- **Signature:** Once returned seed is logged, the timeline's "harvest" band fills in.
- **Avoids:** Static layouts and tables.
- **Tradeoff:** It's the most memorable, but the hardest for a volunteer at the desk who just needs to find a loan quickly. Searching for a loan would jump to its place on the timeline. It's also the most work to build, and also needs the `motion` library.

---

My pick is **B**. It has the motion and layering you asked for, and every animation does real work: returning a packet. Taking A's stamp moment and its row view as B's grid mode would make it easier to scan.

Which do you want: A, B, C, or a mix (for example "B's deck with A's typography")? I'll do the pre-build check and start building once you choose.

runs.name: p2-motion-r2
runs.reply:
Seedkeep now uses the Packet Deck design. I checked it in a real browser at 1280px and 375px, and the build passes. The dev server is still running at http://localhost:5199/.

**What it looks like**
- **Packets on kraft paper:** each loan is drawn as a seed packet in its crop's colour, with a flat crop illustration, a lot number, and the borrower and days out on the bottom flap. They sit in a stack on a kraft-paper background.
- **Deck:** swipe the top packet sideways to leaf through, using the springs and drag-to-tilt feel of Motion's Card Stack. The crop name ("TOMATO", "SWEETCORN") is set large behind the stack and changes as you go.
- **Logging a return:** drag a packet onto the "Seed returned" envelope. It flies in, shrinks and gets a red "SEED RETURNED · 1 OCT" stamp, and an Undo appears next to the controls.
- **Without dragging:** a "Log seed return" button and keyboard support (←/→ to leaf through) do the same job.
- **Spread:** a toggle switches between Deck and a grid of all packets on loan, with an animated rearrange between the two.
- **Kept from before:** search now matches variety, crop or borrower, with helpful empty states. Returned loans are also listed by date under the envelope.

**Review and fixes**
I wrote the pre-build check to `.design/prebuild.md` before any code, then had an independent reviewer judge the screenshots. It flagged eight problems, and I fixed and re-checked all of them:
- On desktop the envelope reacted when the packet was nowhere near it. It now only reacts when the packet is actually over it.
- The large name behind the stack broke into fragments and smeared during swipes. It's now the crop name on one line, swapped without overlap.
- The ← → buttons shifted sideways when the packet name changed.
- The Undo message could be hidden or off-screen.
- Spread mode had seven heavy, identically labelled buttons.
- On mobile the header pushed the deck and button below the first screen.
- The focus ring was a blue that clashed with the palette.
- The grid left a single packet alone on the last row.

Two motion issues were fixed as well: swiped packets now tuck behind the stack instead of fading, and the switch to Spread is slow enough to see. Separately, I darkened the squash packet's orange because its small text was too faint to read comfortably.

**Fidelity to the two references:** the stacked composition, the top packet dominating, the loose tilts, swipe-to-leaf, and the drag physics are kept. Three things changed on purpose: dragging into the envelope logs a return, Spread uses a toggle instead of hover, and the dark photo style became printed packets.

**Things you should know**
- **New dependency:** `motion` (v13.5) for the drag, springs and layout animation. It brings the JS bundle to about 123 kB gzipped.
- **Fonts:** Bricolage Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono load from Google Fonts. Without a network they fall back to system fonts.
- **Sample data:** I expanded it to 10 loans with real heirloom varieties so the deck has depth. Like before, it's in-memory only and nothing is saved.
- **Not tested:** touch drag on a real phone, widths between 375 and 1280, and lint (the repo has no linter set up).
- **Housekeeping:** nothing is committed. Screenshots are in `.playwright-mcp/` and reference previews in `.design/refs/`. I couldn't add those folders to `.git/info/exclude` because that file needs your permission, so add them there or to `.gitignore` before committing.

# Pre-build check — Seedkeep redesign

## Directions considered (research: 21st.dev; Refero/Mobbin not connected)

- **A. Lending ledger** — Energy 2 · Density 3 · Motion 1 · Fidelity high.
  Reference-led: Audit Log Table (status tabs with counts above a ruled
  table) and Invoices data table (title + one-line summary, search beside
  filters, empty state that clears the search).
- **B. Packet drawer** — Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 2 · Fidelity low.
  Loans as kraft seed envelopes filed in a card-catalogue drawer; return
  shown as a rubber date-stamp. References: library date-due slip, seed
  packet back, catalogue drawer label.
- **C. Season board** — Energy 4 · Density 3 · Motion 3 · Fidelity medium.
  Each loan a bar across a March–October growing season, with a harvest
  marker when saved seed comes back.

## Selected

**Mix: A's composition and interaction, with B's visual language.** Chosen by
the agent; the user asked for an autonomous choice. Why: the job is
operational (volunteers find a packet and mark it returned), so the
ledger's scan-and-act structure wins. B's paper, ink and stamp vocabulary
keeps it from reading as a generic SaaS table. C was rejected because a
timeline buries the one action under navigation, and three loans don't fill
a season chart.
Scores carried: composition from A (Energy 2, Density 3, Fidelity high on
composition and interaction), visual treatment from B (Energy 3, Motion 2).

## References as constraints

- Audit Log Table — https://21st.dev/@arihantcodes_1f7b8c4d/components/audit-log-table
  (saved `.playwright-mcp/refs-audit.png`). Adapts: **composition** (filter
  tabs with live counts, then ruled rows) and **interaction model**
  (one-click tab filter combined with text search). Motion: the reference's
  video was not inspected, and the plan doesn't use its motion.
- Invoices data table — https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/data-table-bulk-actions
  (saved `.playwright-mcp/refs-invoice.jpg`). Adapts: **hierarchy** (title,
  then one summary sentence, then toolbar) and **spacing rhythm** (generous
  row height, ~56px). Not taken: checkboxes and bulk bar (no bulk job),
  pagination (tiny dataset), sortable headers.
- Visual treatment: **intentionally changed** from both references (neutral
  grey/white) to B's seed-library paper and ink.

## Check

1. Without logo/copy: ruled ledger paper, a margin rule, and "returned"
   rubber stamps read as a library loan book.
2. Product-specific decisions: (a) the return mark is an ink stamp with the
   return wording, not a pill; (b) the ledger has a numbered entry column and a
   red margin rule like a loan book; (c) dates are typed in mono with a
   "days out this season" count; (d) the summary sentence is in the
   library's own terms ("2 packets still in gardens").
3. At risk of: header over a centered container, pills for status, one accent
   over neutral grey.
4. Avoided: no white cards on grey (rows sit on paper), no status pills, no
   indigo. The masthead is left-aligned and type-led, with no bar.
5. Sections differ: the masthead is display serif and sparse; the toolbar is
   compact and tabbed; the ledger is dense and ruled; the footer is a quiet
   colophon line.
6. Focal point: the ledger's open loans (variety names in serif).
7. Eye path: the wordmark and summary sentence, then the tabs with counts, then
   the first row's variety and its action.
8. Progress: marking a return stamps the row, the counts update, and the row
   dims to inked-in history.
9. Most memorable interaction: the stamp landing on "Mark returned" (a short
   scale and rotate; reduced-motion users get an instant change).
10. Strongest contrast: the deep ink green action buttons and the terracotta stamp
    against cream paper.
11. Flatter than refs? No. It matches A's density and has more texture than
    either reference. Its only motion is the stamp, which is B's level.

## Revised by the check

Status pills were dropped from the plan in favor of the stamp. The status tabs
are styled as ledger index tabs, not a pill segmented control.

# Seedkeep pre-build check

## Selected direction
**B: The Packet Deck**. `Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`. Chosen by the user ("Go with B. Build it.").

## Selected references
- **Motion Card Stack**: https://21st.dev/@motiondotdev/components/motion-card-stack
  (preview `refs/motion-card-stack.webp`, frames `refs/motion-card-stack-frames.png`, source retrieved via get_component).
  *Behavior note:* Trigger is a pointer drag on the top card, x axis only. The card follows the pointer and rotates by its resting tilt plus 10° per 400px of travel.
  It counts as a swipe past half the stack width or a velocity over 50. The card then becomes the back card while its x springs home (stiffness 600, damping 50), and the next card scales up into place.
  Each card's resting tilt is `sin(index) × 5°`. Depth sets z, opacity and scale (0.5→1), animated by a spring (stiffness 600, damping 30). Tap scales to 0.98.
  The reference shows no mobile behavior. Ours drags by touch at ~375 the same way, plus buttons. It has no reduced-motion handling. Ours uses `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`, which drops the transform animations.
- **Layered Stack**: https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack
  (preview `refs/layered-stack.webp`, frames `refs/layered-stack-frames.png`. Source not retrieved because the daily quota is spent.)
  *Behavior note (from video frames):* The trigger is hover (ours uses a Deck/Spread toggle button). Grid tiles converge on the centre with small random rotations, ending as a tight, slightly fanned pile in about 0.5s. The reverse spreads them back into a neat grid. Ours does this with Motion layout animation; at ~375 the grid has 2 columns. Reduced motion means an instant switch.

Adapts → plan constraints:
| Aspect | From | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Composition | Card Stack | On-loan packets are a physical overlapping stack, the stage's centrepiece |
| Hierarchy | Card Stack | Top packet dominant; others peek, scaled and faded by depth |
| Spacing rhythm | Layered Stack | Loose sin-based tilts in the deck; the spread grid keeps a residual ±1.5° tilt |
| Interaction model | both | Horizontal swipe cycles the deck (Card Stack). A Deck↔Spread toggle (Layered Stack) |
| Motion | both | Card Stack's springs and drag→rotate mapping verbatim; layout morph deck↔grid |
| Visual treatment | not taken | Dark photo look replaced by printed seed packets on kraft |

## Answers
1. **Domain without logo/copy?** Yes. Illustrated paper seed packets on kraft, with a "returned seed" envelope, read as a seed library.
2. **Product-specific decisions:** (a) every loan is a seed packet whose colour comes from the crop and which carries a flat crop illustration; (b) the "Seed returned" envelope is the drop target, and returned packets sit tucked into it, peeking out; (c) a date stamp on return; (d) a hand-written borrower flap; (e) "days out" counted as season days.
3. **Most at risk of:** a card grid with pills (the spread mode), the AI default of one accent over neutral, and a centred header over a container.
4. **Drift check:** No white cards on grey. The surface is kraft with coloured packets. Status is shown by placement (deck vs envelope) plus a stamp and text, not pills. There's no metric tiles row. Counts are set in a masthead line.
5. **Section structure:** The masthead is a big condensed wordmark with an inline search. The stage is asymmetric: the deck on the left, a huge outlined variety name layered behind it, and the envelope to the right. The spread mode is a dense grid. Each region differs in scale and surface.

## Visual energy
6. **Focal point:** the top packet of the deck.
7. **Eye path:** the top packet, then the giant variety name behind it, then the envelope with its tucked returned packets.
8. **As you progress:** cycling changes the backdrop name and packet colour. Returns fill the envelope and empty the deck, and an empty deck shows an end-of-season state.
9. **Most memorable interaction:** dragging a packet down into the envelope (or pressing Log return). It flies in via a shared layout transition and is stamped.
10. **Strongest contrast:** the saturated top packet against the kraft and the dark ink backdrop type.
11. **Flatter than the references?** No. The deck keeps Card Stack's physics, and the Spread toggle keeps Layered Stack's morph. The dark photographic look is dropped on purpose for the packet/kraft language the direction specifies.

## Revisions from this check
The spread grid is allowed to become a plain card grid only with a residual tilt, packet styling and no pills. Return is offered as a downward drag plus an explicit button, so keyboard and screen-reader users have the same action.

probe2_build_judge.packet:
Review the rendered Seedkeep redesign. Judge screenshots and the live app, not source.

Product: Seedkeep, the lending tracker for a neighbourhood seed library (Hillside Seed Library). Volunteers record which seed packets are on loan, to whom, since when, and mark them returned when the borrower brings saved seed back at season end. The data held: variety, crop, growing note, borrower, date out, returned date. 10 loans, 3 returned.

User's stated taste: visually rich, expressive interfaces, bold typography, layered composition, real motion. Something people would bookmark for its design, not a plain admin dashboard.

Chosen direction (picked by the user): "B: The Packet Deck". Scores: Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high. It's reference-led.
References (previews saved locally; Read them):
- Motion Card Stack, https://21st.dev/@motiondotdev/components/motion-card-stack. Preview: $PROBE_ROOT/p2-motion/.design/refs/motion-card-stack.webp. Frames: .design/refs/motion-card-stack-frames.png.
  Behavior note: drag the top card on x; it rotates by its resting tilt plus 10° per 400px. Past half the width or a flick, it moves to the back and the next card scales up. Springs: stiffness 600, damping 30/50. Resting tilt is sin(index)·5°.
- Layered Stack, https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack. Preview: .design/refs/layered-stack.webp. Frames: .design/refs/layered-stack-frames.png.
  Behavior note: grid tiles converge into a fanned pile and back, in about 0.5s.
Adapts entries (the direction's constraints):
- composition: on-loan packets as a physical overlapping stack (Card Stack)
- hierarchy: top packet dominant, others peek (Card Stack)
- spacing rhythm: loose tilts in deck, residual tilt in grid (Layered Stack)
- interaction model: swipe sideways to cycle the deck, plus a Deck/Spread toggle (both)
- motion: Card Stack springs and drag-to-rotate; layout morph deck to grid
- visual treatment: not taken (dark photo look replaced by printed seed packets on kraft)
Intentional changes, with reasons: dragging down into the "Seed returned" envelope logs a return (the product's core action), with an explicit button for keyboard and screen-reader users. The deck uses depth-based scale and offset instead of Card Stack's 0.5→1 scale, because with ~7 cards the reference formula hides nearly everything. Toggle instead of hover for Layered Stack, because hover is unavailable on touch and is an accidental trigger.
Product-specific decisions the check named: crop-coloured illustrated seed packets; the returned-seed envelope with returned packets tucked in, stamped; date stamps; the borrower on the packet flap; days-out counts.

Live app: http://localhost:5199/ (dev server running). Views: Deck (default), Spread (toggle), search.

Final screenshots (in $PROBE_ROOT/p2-motion/.playwright-mcp/):
- final-1280-deck.png, final-1280-spread.png, final-1280-empty-search.png (taken just before a copy fix to the right-hand empty message)
- final-375-deck.png, final-375-spread.png
Motion frames, desktop 1280: motion-swipe-mid.png, motion-swipe-after80.png, motion-swipe-settled.png, motion-drop-armed.png, motion-drop-120.png, motion-drop-settled.png, spread-120.png, spread-370.png.
Motion frames, mobile 375: m375-motion-1-swipe-mid.png, m375-motion-2-swipe-settled.png, m375-motion-3-drop-armed-v2.png, m375-motion-4-after-drop-full.png.

Report:
1. Overall visual quality and the most important visual defects, ranked.
2. For each Adapts entry: preserved, intentionally changed, or lost.
3. Motion and interaction fidelity, desktop and mobile separately.
4. Whether the product-specific decisions are visible.
5. Any drift to generic defaults.
Be concrete: viewport, region, and what to change.
probe2_build_judge.report:
I found three high-severity defects. The biggest is that the main gesture, logging a return by dragging, doesn't line up with where the envelope actually is on desktop. Overall the build is strong: it reads like the Hillside Seed Library's own desk and not a SaaS template, and the direction mostly held.

## 1. Defects, ranked

**1. High: on desktop the envelope accepts the packet before the packet is anywhere near it.** In `motion-drop-armed.png` the packet is dragged straight down over the Log button and the hint, yet the envelope already says "LET GO TO FILE IT" about 200px away, up and to the right. The hint says "drag down into the envelope", but at 1280 the envelope is beside the deck, not below it. At 375 "down" is correct, but the envelope starts below the first screen (`review-375-deck.png`, 812px tall), so you can't see the drop target when the page loads.
- Fix: on desktop, only arm the envelope when the packet is actually over it (or change the hint to "toward the envelope"). On mobile, make sure the envelope's lip shows in the first screen.
- Confidence: high.

**2. High: the large faded variety name behind the deck breaks up into unreadable pieces.**
- `final-1280-deck.png`: the back cards hide "PURPLE", leaving a purple block poking out at the left edge (x≈230, y≈355–445).
- On mobile, the top half of "PURPLE" is cut off.
- During a swipe the old and new names fade over each other into a smear: "CHEROKEE" with "LEMON" (`motion-swipe-after80.png`), "LEMON" with "GOLDEN BANTAM" (`motion-drop-120.png`).
- Yellow "LEMON" on kraft is barely visible.
- It repeats the name already printed on the top packet. Restraint says remove it. If you keep it, fit it on one line fully above the stack and swap names without overlap.
- Confidence: high.

**3. Medium: the ← and → buttons jump sideways when you change packets.** The Log button's width follows the variety name: the arrows sit at x 137/590 for Cherokee Purple and 187/540 for Lemon (`review-arrow.png`). Clicking → repeatedly misses. Fix: give the button a fixed width. Confidence: high.

**4. Medium: the Undo message shows up in two different places.**
- In the desktop deck it covers the controls: the button and → are hidden in `motion-drop-settled.png`.
- In Spread and on mobile it appears inside the returned list. At 375 that is about 500px below the deck, so you can't see Undo right after the drop (`m375-motion-4-after-drop-full.png`).
- Fix: use one position, next to the envelope, that is visible from the deck and doesn't cover controls.
- Confidence: high.

**5. Medium: Spread repeats seven identical black "Log seed return" buttons.** They are the heaviest shapes on the page and compete with the packets (`final-1280-spread.png`, `final-375-spread.png`). Their screen-reader names are also identical, with no variety name. Fix: put a lighter return action on each packet's borrower flap, labelled with the variety. Confidence: medium.

**6. Medium: on mobile the first screen is mostly header.** The header takes about 335 of 812px, the packet is cut off at the bottom, and neither the Log button nor the envelope is visible. Fix: put the stats on one line, and search and the Deck/Spread toggle on one row. At 1280×800 the hint is also cut off (`review-1280-deck.png`). Confidence: high.

**7. Low: the focus ring is saturated blue**, the only blue anywhere in the kraft-and-ink palette. On the deck it is a straight rectangle around a tilted packet (`review-focus-2.png`, `review-focus-4.png`). Use the dark ink colour or the stamp red. Confidence: high.

**8. Low: Spread at 1280 has two layouts in the screenshots.** It shows 3 columns with an orphaned seventh packet and a large empty area (`final-1280-spread.png`), versus 4 columns (`spread-370.png`). The cause is unclear. Confidence: low.

## 2. Each adapted aspect
- **Composition, overlapping stack:** preserved (`final-1280-deck.png`).
- **Hierarchy, top packet dominant:** preserved. The depth-based scale is the change you named. Only about 3 back cards peek out.
- **Spacing rhythm:** preserved. Loose tilts in the deck, slight leftover tilt in Spread (Cherokee Purple, Black Krim).
- **Interaction model:** swipe and the toggle are preserved. Drag-to-return is the change you named, but its geometry is broken (defect 1).
- **Motion:** drag-to-rotate is preserved. Swipe to the back is partly lost: the swiped packet fades to a see-through ghost off to the right (`motion-swipe-after80.png`) instead of visibly tucking behind the stack. The deck-to-grid change is mostly lost: at 120ms (`spread-120.png`) packets are already almost in place, and my keyboard toggle captured only the end state. The reference's visible converge-and-fan over about 0.5s can't be seen.
- **Visual treatment:** changed as intended, to printed packets on kraft, and done well.

## 3. Motion and interaction fidelity
- **Desktop:** drag rotation and cycling are faithful, and arrow keys cycle the deck. The drop arms in the wrong place, the move to the back fades instead of tucking, and the grid change isn't observable.
- **Mobile:** the swipe reads well, with the packet swinging off-screen to the right as in the reference (`m375-motion-1-swipe-mid.png`). The downward drop matches the layout, but only after scrolling. The Undo is off-screen afterwards.

## 4. Product-specific decisions
All five are visible:
- crop-coloured illustrated packets;
- the envelope with returned packets tucked in, stamped "SEED RETURNED 18 SEPT";
- date stamps;
- the borrower on the packet flap;
- days-out counts.

## 5. Drift to generic defaults
There is little. The look holds: printed packets with lot numbers sitting in a kraft returns envelope is something only a seed library would build. What did drift is the browser-default blue focus ring, the generic black-bar Undo message, and Spread's repeated buttons.

## Not verified
- The empty-search right-hand message after the copy fix: I can't type.
- The flight of a dropped packet into the envelope, and whether spring timing matches stiffness 600.
- Dragging in Spread.
- Hover states in the deck.
- Loading and error states.
- A flick throw.
- Touch drag on a real device.
- Widths between 375 and 1280.

My screenshots are in `$PROBE_ROOT/p2-motion/`: `review-1280-deck.png`, `review-arrow.png`, `review-focus-2.png`, `review-focus-4.png`, `review-spread-early.png`, `review-375-deck.png`.

probe2_orchestrator_motion_check.method: After the build finished, the orchestrating session served the final build (vite, port 5299) and recorded it with Playwright recordVideo in new contexts at 1280x800 and 375x812: a 360 px (1280) or 240 px (375) mouse drag right on the top packet over about 300 ms, release, 1.5 s wait, click Spread, 1.5 s wait. Frames were extracted with ffmpeg at 10 and 30 fps; boards/gate-hardening-motion-frames.jpg holds the 30 fps strips.
observed: Swipe, both widths: after release the swiped packet slides back behind the new top packet within a few frames at 30 fps, on the order of 100 ms; it does not fade out in place. The recording's frames and the script's time marks are not aligned to the frame, so durations are approximate.

Spread, both widths: the pile opens into the grid over about 6 frames at 30 fps (roughly 200 ms), each frame showing packets between positions. The build's own behavior note puts Layered Stack's transition at about 0.5 s.

375: the deck, the arrows and the Log seed return button are in the first 812 px; the envelope's top edge shows at the bottom. The first morph frame at 375 shows several packets' Log return buttons overlapping in the pile for one frame.

probe2_fact_check_notes: The build's Layered Stack behavior note (from video frames) has hover gathering the grid into a pile; 21st's description of component 26717 is 'fans children into a shuffled deck and re-stacks them into a neat grid on hover', and the reference fidelity probe's fetched source agrees. The Motion Card Stack note matches its retrieved source.
The judge's two motion losses are under its desktop verdict, from 1280 frames; at 375 it called the swipe faithful and did not assess the spread.
The judge pressed ArrowRight, Shift+Tab and Enter itself; it cannot drag.
